pll1d12c2-d1e3477.summary: Takes up the second question: whether the Spirit proceeds more fully or more from the Father than from the Son.

pll1d12c2-d1e3480.summary: Answers that the Spirit proceeds neither earlier nor more fully from the Father. But Augustine says the Spirit proceeds 'principally' from the Father, from whom the Word is begotten and the Spirit principally proceeds.
claims: The Spirit does not proceed more fully from the Father than from the Son.
Augustine says the Spirit proceeds principally from the Father.

pll1d12c2-d1e3499.summary: Gives Augustine's own explanation: he added 'principally' because the Spirit also proceeds from the Son, but the Father gave the Son this, not to an already existing Son, but by begetting him, so that the common Gift would proceed from him too. So 'principally' means that the Son has from the Father that the Spirit proceeds from him.
claims: The Father gave the Son, in begetting him, that the Spirit proceeds from him.
'Principally' does not mean earlier or more.

pll1d12c2-d1e3512.summary: Adds that in the same sense the Spirit is said to proceed 'properly' from the Father.

pll1d12c2-d1e3517.summary: Cites Jerome's exposition of the faith: the Spirit proceeds properly from the Father, is properly from the Father, and truly proceeds from the Father.
claims: Jerome says the Spirit is properly from the Father.

pll1d12c2-d1e3553.summary: Interprets Jerome: the Spirit is 'properly' from the Father not because he proceeds earlier or more fully from him, but because the Father has from himself that the Spirit proceeds from him, while the Son has it from the Father.
claims: The Father has from himself that the Spirit proceeds from him.
The Son has from the Father that the Spirit proceeds from him.

pll1d12c2-d1e3556.summary: Suggests that the same sense explains why the Spirit is said to be sent and to be from the Father through the Son.

pll1d12c2-d1e3559.summary: Cites Hilary addressing the Father: 'your Holy Spirit, coming forth from you and sent through him.'
claims: Hilary says the Spirit comes from the Father and is sent through the Son.

pll1d12c2-d1e3580.summary: Further Hilary: the only-begotten, born before time, remains, so that the Spirit is from the Father through him. Hilary admits he does not grasp this by sense but holds it in conscience, being dull in spiritual things.
claims: The Spirit is from the Father through the Son.
This is held by faith beyond understanding.

pll1d12c2-d1e3592.summary: Further Hilary's prayer to keep the faith of his baptismal creed, worshipping the Father and the Son and meriting the Spirit who is from the Father through the only-begotten.
claims: The Spirit is from the Father through the only-begotten.

pll1d12c2-d1e3604.summary: Interprets Hilary: 'through the Son' does not mean through a lesser Son, but that the Spirit is from and sent by both, and the Son has this from the Father. Hilary made this distinction in speech to show that authority is in the Father.
claims: 'Through the Son' does not imply the Son is lesser.
The Spirit is from and sent by both Father and Son.
Hilary's phrasing shows the Father's authority.

pll1d12c2-d1e3612.summary: Explains that because the Father is the author of the procession by which the Spirit proceeds from the Son, Christ said 'he proceeds from the Father' (John 15:26), although he proceeds from both.
claims: Christ named the Father in John 15:26 because the Father is author of the procession.

pll1d12c2-d1e3624.summary: Gives Augustine's fuller explanation: Christ refers to the Father what is his own, as with 'my doctrine is not mine.' From whom the Son has his being God, he has that the Spirit proceeds from him. As the Father timelessly gave the Son 'life in himself' (John 5:26), not to a Son already living, he gave him that the Spirit should proceed from him as from the Father, with no before or after.
claims: The Son refers to the Father what is his own.
The Son has from the Father that the Spirit proceeds from him.
The Father gave this to the Son timelessly, in begetting him.
There is no before or after in the processions.

pl-l1d12c2.summary: Asks whether the Spirit proceeds more fully or more from the Father than from the Son, and answers no. Augustine's 'principally from the Father' and Jerome's 'properly from the Father' mean that the Father has from himself that the Spirit proceeds from him, while the Son has this from the Father, by being begotten. Likewise Hilary's 'from the Father through the Son' does not make the Son lesser but marks the Father's authority. This also explains why Christ says the Spirit 'proceeds from the Father' (John 15:26): he refers to the Father what is his own. With Augustine, as the Father timelessly gave the Son life in himself, he gave him that the Spirit should proceed from him.
claims: The Spirit does not proceed more fully or more from the Father than from the Son.
'Principally' and 'properly from the Father' mean that the Father has from himself, and the Son from the Father, that the Spirit proceeds from them.
The Son received from the Father, in being begotten, that the Spirit proceeds from him.
'From the Father through the Son' marks the Father's authority, not the Son's inferiority.
Christ's 'proceeds from the Father' refers to the Father what is the Son's own.
There is no before and after in the processions.
